scientific_claim: On an immutable repo-owned real UTF-8 prose/code split, the existing Wingless raw-byte substrate learned a fixed 256-entry four-byte motif layer without tokenization. On held-out files it covered at least 10.33% of evaluable positions, improved motif-covered next-byte accuracy by at least 0.518, reduced effective event count by at least 14.64%, and improved overall bits-per-byte by at least 0.0535 relative to the one-byte-context baseline, with exact train/eval blob identity and no capacity growth.
next_question: Can the real-byte motif layer support a second learned hierarchy level and preserve its predictive/efficiency gains across a larger immutable prose/code corpus and stronger cross-file distribution shift?
scope: small immutable real UTF-8 repository corpus; not open-domain language competence
